chunks: Ali ibn Abdillah al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Mehzayar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal Sahib al-Taq, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever would love to be the noblest of people, let him fear Allah. Whoever would love to be the most God-fearing of people, let him rely upon Allah. Whoever would love to be the richest of people, let him have more trust in what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than in what is in his own hand.

Then he (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Shall I not tell you about the worst of people? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He who hates the people and is hated by the people. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of someone worse than this? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He who does not dismiss an offense, does not accept an excuse, and does not forgive a sin. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of someone worse than this? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He from whose evil people are not safe, and whose good is not even hoped for.

Indeed, Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) stood among the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel! Do not impart wisdom to fools, for you will have oppressed it; and do not withhold it from its people, for you will have oppressed them; and do not assist the oppressor in his oppression, for your virtue will become void.

Matters are three: a matter whose rightness is apparent to you, so follow it; a matter whose misguidance is apparent to you, so avoid it; and a matter that is disagreed upon, so relegate it to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أتقى: The most God-fearing, the one with the most taqwa
key_terms.أغنى: The richest, wealthiest -- here in a spiritual sense
key_terms.أكرم الناس: The noblest of people, one with the highest honor
key_terms.عثرة: A stumble, slip, or offense -- refers to human mistakes
key_terms.غيه: Its misguidance, error, deviation from truth
key_terms.معذرة: An excuse or apology offered for wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the noblest and worst of people?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Sadiq from his forefathers, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) first teaches three paths to nobility, God-consciousness, and spiritual wealth -- all achieved through taqwa, tawakkul, and trust in God respectively. He then progressively describes three levels of the worst people, culminating in one whose evil is feared and whose good is not hoped for. The hadith concludes with a saying attributed to Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS) addressed to the Children of Israel about the proper handling of wisdom and a tripartite classification of all matters into the clearly right, the clearly wrong, and the ambiguous -- the last of which should be referred to God.
